task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the extension of the residential parking zone in Reedharbor. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Reedharbor Council will add eight blocks to its existing six-block residential parking zone, creating a 14-block zone.
The extension takes effect Nov. 9, 2026, after signs and curb markings are installed.
The zone's permit requirement applies from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on weekdays, not around the clock.
The annual resident permit remains $35, and the decision does not increase that fee.
A permit allows use of eligible spaces within the zone but does not reserve a particular space or guarantee that one is available.
The added area contains 176 ordinary curb spaces, according to the city's marking plan.
The city has not supplied a count of how many of those spaces are occupied by residents rather than commuters on a typical day.
Residents petitioned for the extension after a nearby office complex expanded its occupied floor area without changing the city's parking-zone boundary.
Transport manager Reva Linn said, "The permit changes who can use a space at certain times; it does not create a space."
Eligible households in the new blocks may begin applying Oct. 12, using the city's existing address-verification process.
Guest permits will remain available under the current visitor scheme, which has not been expanded to cover all-day commuter parking.
Loading bays and marked accessible spaces retain their existing arrangements and are not converted into ordinary permit spaces.
A group of nearby shop workers asked the city to examine where displaced employee parking might move.
Shop worker representative Dena Wren said, "A boundary can solve a problem on one side and move it to the next street."
The council will survey the streets immediately outside the expanded zone before and after implementation.
That survey is planned work, and the city has not yet concluded that parking displacement will or will not occur.
Drivers will receive warning notices during the first 30 calendar days of the extension before routine penalty notices begin under the supplied rollout plan.
The warning period does not suspend existing restrictions on blocking entrances, loading bays or accessible spaces.
The street signs will use a different border color for the zone but retain the existing permit symbol.
The city budget includes $28,400 for signs, road markings and processing the first round of new applications.
No new off-street parking facility or employee shuttle is included in the approved package.
The council has scheduled a six-month review that can consider boundary changes but does not automatically expand the zone further.

forbidden_additions: A reserved or guaranteed resident space, higher permit fee or 24-hour restriction.
Completed displacement findings or funded new parking.
A warning period described as suspending every parking restriction.
preserve: Eligibility to park distinguished from the supply of spaces.
The extension's hours, rollout and concerns outside its boundary.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
